title: A Surgical Protocol for Precise High-Throughput and Precise Viral Injections in Rhesus Monkey Brain
author: Anne Claire Tangen

steps.title: Print and assemble circuit holder
steps.instruction: 3‑D print the injection circuit holder in Accura ClearVue (EtO‑compatible) using the supplied STL file, then attach the metal bar with Phillips flat‑head screw (4‑40, 5/16″) and hex nut, verifying a secure, non‑rotating connection.

steps.title: Prepare injector needles
steps.instruction: Sharpen a 30‑gauge hypodermic needle to a 30° bevel (or use a pre‑sharpened needle), cut it to 70 mm length; cut a 23‑gauge needle to 50 mm length and place it as a guide tube around the 30‑gauge needle to prevent bending.

steps.title: Cut and connect PEEK tubing
steps.instruction: Cut 50 cm of 1/16″ PEEK tubing with a plastic tubing cutter (flat, burr‑free), connect one end to the CapTite Interconnect Elbow using a CapTite One‑Piece Fitting (Ferrule), and secure the elbow in the 3‑D printed holder with Phillips rounded‑head screws (2‑56, 5/16″) and hex nuts (2‑56).

steps.title: Assemble top piece and fittings
steps.instruction: Attach the top piece of the 3‑D printed holder with socket head screws (4‑40, 3/8″ long), hex nuts (4‑40), Phillips rounded‑head screws (2‑56, 5/16″) and hex nuts (2‑56); then attach an Idex Fingertight One‑Piece Fitting to the free end of the PEEK tubing.

steps.title: Add Idex adapters and drill tubing
steps.instruction: Connect the Idex fitting to an Idex Threaded Adapter (PEEK, 0.020″ ID, 10‑32 coned to 1/4‑28 flat bottom), slide the tubing out ≥5 mm before screwing, cut a ~5 mm piece of PEEK tubing, drill a 0.6 mm hole through it, and insert the 23‑gauge needle into this tubing.

steps.title: Complete needle‑tube assembly
steps.instruction: Place the needle‑in‑PEEK assembly into the Idex Fingertight fitting (narrow side outward), screw the assembly into the coned side of the Idex Threaded Adapter, attach a Hamilton 100 µL syringe to the flat‑bottom side, and verify all connections by gently pulling on the tubing.

steps.title: Prime circuit with distilled water
steps.instruction: Load the syringe with distilled water via the loading connector, inject water through the circuit to confirm no clogs and check for leaks; tighten PEEK connectors only finger‑tight to avoid cracks, and keep the needle tip straight and sharp.

steps.title: Frame animal in stereotaxic device
steps.instruction: Secure one ear bar in the ear canal, feeling the zygomatic arch; place the second ear bar in the contralateral canal; align and center both ear bars by loosening locking screws, confirming matching numbers; attach orbit holder and mouthpiece, tighten AP adjustment screw, record ear‑bar and orbit‑holder positions, and place a tooth marker on a canine tooth.

steps.title: Determine stereotaxic coordinates
steps.instruction: Using pre‑operative sagittal MRI slices, identify the Y‑coordinate of the ear‑bar tips; for each target, read X, Y, Z of the injection site and of the sagittal sinus on the same coronal slice; during surgery calculate Y relative to ear‑bar zero and X/Z using the sinus as reference; use the provided Excel sheet (Supplementary file 3) to compute final coordinates.

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and circuit
steps.instruction: Sterilize surgical instruments, injection circuits, loading connectors, spare components, micro‑injection syringes, Allen wrenches, micro‑injection pumps, micromanipulators, and ear bars (≈15 h total). If EtO is used for the circuit, flush the entire tubing with a chemical sterilant and rinse thoroughly with sterile distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare circuit dead volume with mineral oil
steps.instruction: Under sterile conditions, attach the loading connector to the syringe, draw sterile mineral oil into the syringe and tubing, push/pull the plunger several times to eliminate bubbles, draw ~20 µL oil, wipe the needle tip (without removing the connector), then withdraw the required viral volume; finally, create a 10 µL air gap by pulling back the plunger, ensuring no liquid remains in the needle or connector.

steps.title: Administer peri‑operative medications
steps.instruction: Give dexamethasone 0.5 mg/kg IM the evening before surgery; on surgery day give 0.5 mg/kg IM TID for 3 days, then BID for 2 days, SID for 1 day, and 0.25 mg/kg SID for 1 day. Give cefazolin 25 mg/kg IM the evening before and BID for 3 days, then switch to cephalexin 25 mg/kg PO BID for 11 days. Give meloxicam 0.2 mg/kg IM SID for 3 days, then PO SID for 3 days.

steps.title: Zero stereotaxic frame and attach circuit
steps.instruction: Place sterilized ear bars in the frame at the MRI‑derived distance, keep ear‑bar tips sterile; using the micromanipulator, move the needle tip until it aligns with the center of an ear‑bar and record coordinates; attach the injection circuit to the micromanipulator and mount the micromanipulators on the stereotaxic arms.

steps.title: Sedate, transport, and prepare animal
steps.instruction: Sedate with ketamine 5–15 mg/kg IM and midazolam 0.05–0.2 mg/kg IM, transport to the OR, shave head and neck, perform a rough scrub, place an IV catheter (saphenous or cephalic), intubate, and collect CBC and serum biochemistry.

steps.title: Administer mannitol and maintain IV fluids
steps.instruction: Give mannitol 2 g/kg of 20 % solution IV over 20 min, 2–3 times during surgery as needed; infuse lactated Ringer’s 3–5 mL/kg/h to keep the catheter patent.

steps.title: Monitor physiological parameters
steps.instruction: Continuously monitor heart rate, ECG, end‑tidal CO₂, respiratory rate, blood pressure, body temperature, and MAC; connect to a ventilator if required to maintain stable respiration.

steps.title: Skin preparation and draping
steps.instruction: Place 10–20 sterile 4×4 gauzes in two bowls (one with 70 % ethanol, one with surgical scrub such as povidone‑iodine); protect eyes with dry sterile gauze; scrub the scalp in concentric circles with scrub‑soaked gauze, rinse with ethanol‑soaked gauze, repeat at least three times; disinfect stereotaxic frame arms with fresh gauze; apply sterile antiseptic (e.g., DuraPrep) and allow to dry; scrub hands, don sterile gown and gloves; cover lights with disposable sterile covers; mark sagittal midline and incision boundaries (rostral at brow ridge, caudal ≥20 mm posterior to occipital ridge).

steps.title: Apply surgical drapes
steps.instruction: Place three disposable utility drapes: two parallel to the midline ~20 mm apart for skin stretching, and one anterior to the rostral incision mark; secure with towel clamps if needed; add a craniotomy drape aligning its adhesive edge with the anterior incision mark, press firmly to eliminate air bubbles; optionally use an antimicrobial incision drape (e.g., 3M™ Ioban™) and cover the whole field with a larger drape having a circular opening; avoid touching non‑sterile surfaces while draping.

steps.title: Set up suction, cautery, and instruments
steps.instruction: Connect suction tip to hose and collection canister; plug in disposable cautery pen and verify function; place two surgical bowls and a bulb syringe with sterile saline on the Mayo stand; arrange all instruments needed for the opening phase on the Mayo stand.

steps.title: Make sagittal skin incision
steps.instruction: Using a #10 blade, make a single midline sagittal incision from the brow ridge to at least 20 mm posterior to the occipital ridge, keeping the blade in continuous motion; use thumb and index finger to keep the wound slightly open; maintain the galea by inspecting the first few millimetres and adjusting depth; apply pressure with sterile gauze for hemostasis if bleeding occurs.

steps.title: Separate skin and galea
steps.instruction: Using tissue forceps and periosteal elevators, gently separate skin from galea ~20 mm from the incision line; alternatively, use the curved edge of the #10 blade to dissect along the skin‑galea interface; place scalp clamps to secure drapes and assist hemostasis.

steps.title: Open and retract galea
steps.instruction: Cut through the galea with the periosteal elevator or a #15 blade; then use the elevator or closed Mayo scissors to spread the galea laterally, applying traction; use dry gauze to push the galea laterally as needed.

steps.title: Retract temporalis muscles
steps.instruction: Detach dorsal temporalis tendons from the skull with the sharp edge of a periosteal elevator, keeping the elevator sagittal; elevate tendons to fully separate them; then detach the temporalis muscle body using muscle curettes or the elevator with controlled horizontal movements.

steps.title: Create craniotomy
steps.instruction: Measure craniotomy margins to extend ~10 mm beyond planned injection sites (AP relative to ear‑bar level, ML from midline); for bilateral injections make symmetric margins; use an ultrasonic piezoelectric bone cutter or circular cutting wheel to drill, leaving a thin bone layer over the dura; avoid drilling completely over the sagittal sinus.

steps.title: Lift bone flap and achieve hemostasis
steps.instruction: Using two periosteal elevators, gradually lift the bone flap starting caudally, monitoring for dural adhesions; gently separate adhesions without damaging dura; remove the flap; irrigate the dura; if minor bleeding persists, apply a small surgical patty; for significant hemorrhage, use gel‑foam; remove any patty before closure.

steps.title: Prepare bone flap for replacement
steps.instruction: Remove residual dural adhesions, then drill four suture holes (~3 mm from craniotomy edge) on the skull (two lateral, two caudal) using a bore drill angled slightly; create corresponding holes on the bone flap; smooth sharp edges with rongeurs and apply bone wax (remove excess before dura opening).

steps.title: Measure sagittal sinus and set micromanipulator
steps.instruction: Immediately after bone flap removal, measure the sagittal sinus position; mount the micromanipulator with injection circuit onto the stereotaxic bars; cut through drapes if needed; position the micromanipulator at the most caudal target AP coordinate, set coarse AP position, set fine AP dial to zero; adjust ML and DV until the needle tip gently contacts the middle of the sagittal sinus; record ML and DV; repeat for each target along the AP axis.

steps.title: Open dura mater
steps.instruction: Make a 5 mm margin from craniotomy edges; using a #11 blade on a #7 handle, make a small nick in the dura with the blade back parallel to the cortex; lift the nicked edge with fine forceps; penetrate further with the #11 blade or iris scissors, keeping tips away from cortex; continue incision with scissors held 1–2 mm open, gliding along the dura; avoid injuring the sagittal sinus at rostral and caudal ends.

steps.title: Prime injection circuit with virus
steps.instruction: Initiate virus efflux at a high flow rate (10–20 µL/min) to fill dead volume; then reduce to 1–5 µL/min until viral fluid is seen at the needle tip; stop flow or set to a very low rate (0.01 µL/min).

steps.title: Perform viral injection
steps.instruction: After AP/ML positioning, lower the needle just above the cortical surface, inspect for large vessels and adjust if needed; gently penetrate cortex (maintaining minimal flow ~0.01 µL/min if desired); advance to target DV coordinate; set injection pump to the intended rate (as per Table 1); irrigate cortex with sterile saline every 2–3 min; inject virus; wait 10 min before withdrawing; retract needle slowly over the first 2–3 mm; confirm viral flow after withdrawal; for multiple injections along one track, proceed from ventral to superficial sites with a 1‑min wait between injections.

steps.title: Close surgical site
steps.instruction: Remove micromanipulators, flush cortical surface with normal saline; close dura with 5‑0 or 6‑0 absorbable/non‑absorbable monofilament sutures (1–1.5 mm apart) using a simple continuous pattern; replace bone flap by threading 3‑0 or 2‑0 absorbable sutures through pre‑drilled holes, tying square knots and alternating tension; smooth bone edges with rongeurs and apply bone wax if needed; close galea with 3‑0 absorbable sutures in a continuous pattern (3–4 mm spacing); close skin with 3‑0 (or 2‑0) monofilament absorbable sutures in an intradermal pattern or with a horizontal mattress pattern (2 mm from margin, 4 mm apart); note that non‑absorbable skin sutures are removed after 10–14 days.

steps.title: Post‑operative recovery and monitoring
steps.instruction: After extubation, place the animal in an ICU with heat and supplemental O₂, monitor continuously until consciousness returns; provide oral rehydration drink, then moistened chow and fruit with free water; monitor twice daily for neurological signs; keep the animal in ICU for a minimum of 3 days (brain swelling peaks 48–72 h).

steps.title: Perfuse and extract brain (2‑week endpoint)
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal, perform transcardial perfusion with chilled, fully oxygenated ssACSF (1.5–2 L, 100 mL/min) after inserting a large‑bore olive‑tip cannula into the left ventricle and advancing to the ascending aorta; clamp descending aorta; open thorax, diaphragm, pericardium, and right atrium; excise the heart apex to access left ventricle; turn animal prone, remove bone flaps with rongeurs; dissect dura, falx cerebri, and tentorium; transect cervical spinal cord and cranial nerves; remove brain caudal‑to‑rostral, preserving attachments.

steps.title: Block and store brain tissue
steps.instruction: Immediately place the brain in a brain mold and continuously irrigate with cold, oxygenated ssACSF; cut coronal slabs using the mold (starting at the most rostral region), hemisect, and optionally block individual structures; transfer tissue blocks to sealed containers with cold oxygenated ssACSF.

steps.title: Slice preparation for electrophysiology
steps.instruction: Adhere brain blocks to a specimen stage with cyanoacrylate, section at 250–400 µm on a vibratome (e.g., Leica VT‑1200S) in ice‑cold oxygenated ssACSF; transfer slices to a submerged incubation chamber with oxygenated ssACSF warmed to 32–34 °C for 30 min, then keep at room temperature; allow at least 1 h recovery before electrophysiological recording; replace incubation solution as needed.

steps.title: Validate injection success
steps.instruction: Perform post‑operative MRI with manganese‑enhanced contrast to visualize hyperintense regions at target sites; confirm viral expression after 6–8 weeks via immunohistochemistry and electrophysiology as described in the validation figures.
